gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the OXO 11-in turntable it recommended has only a 9¼-in loading surface, 71% of its footprint (about 67 sq in, or $0.25 per usable sq in at $16.99). By TidyStow's own opening-minus-2-in rule it also needs a cabinet opening or shelf depth of at least 13 in, so it is too big for the 12-in upper cabinet TidyStow sizes at 10 in.
standout_why: Compared against TidyStow 'Lazy Susan Sizes' (cited in both chats) and SimpleHomeNest 'Lazy Susan for Cabinet' (ranks 14 and 18). TidyStow gives the general rule (opening minus 2 in; 12-in upper cabinet takes a 10-in turntable) but never applies it to a product and never separates outer diameter from usable surface. SimpleHomeNest has no sizing, load or price figures at all; its body lists unrelated Amazon home goods. Neither page gives cost per usable square inch for any turntable. Rivals have the rule, so they hold part of the gap; the product-level numbers are new.
decides: It changes the default pick for a standard upper kitchen cabinet. ChatGPT's first card, the OXO 11-in, fails the sizing rule from a page ChatGPT itself got for a 12-in-deep cabinet. The page should send 12-in cabinets to a turntable of about 10 in or smaller, keep the OXO 11-in for openings and depths of 13 in or more, and state that the OXO's real loading surface is 9¼ in, not 11 in.
